checks.claim: sum outward andreturn times solves echodistance
two opposite sensors directpath has nohalf factor
toy3s observed with1s delay at4mpersec gives4m

records.figureReview: No figure in the complete original; learner is asked to construct a system-boundary sketch, not to read unprovided numeric scales.
records.manualArithmetic: Source asks model selection from the physical event, not a numerical exercise. Sum echo travel times d/v+d/v to obtain d=v*duration/2; direct opposite-sensor path gives d=v*duration. Reviewer4m/s,3s yields12m direct and6m echo. If observation includes1s sensor delay, the echo distance is4m instead; the source explicitly distinguishes sensor response. One minute is60s. A variable instantaneous speed needs an integral or a specified average, not an unqualified product. These are constructed reviewer cases, not evidence of student diagnosis or mastery.
records.pedagogicalReview: Connects measurement unit, physical system and event before equation choice; repeated varied cases are suggested ratherthan diagnosing from one failure. Reviewer fixtures do not certify student calibration.
records.physicalAssumptions: Identified system/event and matching units; uniform speed for the stated product, fixed reflector/coincident stationary sender/receiver for simple echo. Response delay not automatically propagation. No inference of student difficulty from one wrong answer, as source explicitly warns.

checks.claim: area times mean normalspeed is volumeflow
uniform normal beam intensity timesarea ispower
balance mass divided density recovers volume
same density steady massbalance gives equal volumeflow
no accumulation implies signed currents sumzero

records.figureReview: No figure in the complete original; drawing signed transport arrows is a suggested reasoning procedure. No missing external numerical simulation is invoked.
records.manualArithmetic: Volume, charge and energy per second yield m³/s,A,W respectively despite sharing a time denominator. Integrating a normal velocity profile over the section gives Qv=S*vbar, where vbar is the area mean normal velocity; uniform normal intensity gives receivedP=I*S. Mass collection converts tovolume only through density. Reviewer6units/3s gives2 in each appropriate dimension; area2m²*3m/s gives6m³/s, while2m²*3W/m² gives6W. Conservation is incoming-minus-outgoing equals accumulation. Tank3in/2out stores1m³/s; a chosen charge-storing boundary3Ain/2Aout stores1C/s. Include capacitor branch current to retain Kirchhoff balance rather than declaring KCL invalid. Different densities can preserve massflow without equal volumeflow, outside the incompressible premise.
records.pedagogicalReview: Shared area/time structure is contrasted with distinct transported quantities anddimensions. Chosen arrows support signed balance and explicit storage checks; doesnotidentifycharge/currentwithenergy/power.
records.physicalAssumptions: Incompressible liquid and cross-sectional area-mean normal velocity for Qv=S*vbar. Uniform normal beam and small receiving area forP=I*S. Volume/mass distinctions requiredensity. Steady boundary with no relevant accumulation for equal incoming/outgoing sums; include all branches or storage terms in a transient. Source is a sufficient steady model, not a claim KCL stops applying to a complete circuit with capacitors.

checks.claim: electrical voltage current duration has energyunits

records.figureReview: CompleteXML/render ofC6-pendenza.svg: energyvertical,timehorizontal. Risingline(105,160)to(260,78), thenhorizontalto(427,78);positive physicalslope thenzero. Labels heating/constantenergy agree. No numericaxisunit calibration; captionnetbalance andfooterpowerinwatts aredimensionallyconsistent.
records.manualArithmetic: Source actual relations are symbolic. Constant electricalP=V*i overduration gives Ein=V*i*duration, and useful fractioneta gives DeltaT=eta*Ein/(mass*c) when phase/capacity changes and other storage are absent. Reviewer6V*2A*2s gives24J; quarter useful gives6J, heating capacity2J/K by3K. Dividing byquarter instead gives96J and exposes an invalid energy gain. Celsius increments andkelvin increments agree; minutes need60 conversion. Liftingmgh is energy and inputminususeful islost/storedoutsideusefulsystem. E(t)=Einitial+P*t has slopeP; a plateau haszero netP, compatible with nonzeroequal5Win/5Wout. The qualitativeSVG has no calibrated numbers and supports these signs, not a numerical heating rate. Variablepower requiresintegration, not the constant shortcut.
records.pedagogicalReview: Boundary and energy arrows precede equations, efficiency is usefulfraction, timeunits/energyupperbound are sanitychecks. Slope isnet power andsource caption explicitlypermitszero netbalance, avoiding the claim a plateau mustbe isolated.
records.physicalAssumptions: Positive input electricalpower by chosen energy-arrow convention, constant productV*i overinterval. Usefulfraction0<=eta<=1 without additional unmodelled energy sources. Constant mass/specificheat, no phasechange or materialtemperature dependence inmcDeltaT model. System boundary specifies container/loss/storage; thermal isolation isnot a denial of electrical work input. Energyplateau meansnet balancezero, not absenceoftransfer.

records.figureReview: No figure in the complete original; three-reading arithmetic and multiplicative patterns are explicit textdata, not inferred from a drawing.
records.manualArithmetic: Actual qualitative halving comparisons: Q proportional r⁴ gives1/16; I proportional1/d² gives4 when distancehalves, with other parameters fixed. Source80,60,40 differencesare-20,-20;80,40,20 ratiosare1/2,1/2. Equal-layer transmissions and equal-time survivals multiply, with dimensionless mu*x orlambda_d*t and initialfractionone. The text says three points suggest models and must be checked against mechanism; exact counterexamples confirm nonuniqueness: addingn(n-1)(n-2) to80-20n matches firstthree points but differsby6 atn3; quadratic80-50n+10n² matches80,40,20 but gives20 ratherthan10next. No arbitrary exponential/log decimal evaluation is assigned.
records.pedagogicalReview: Identifies held variables before scaling and distinguishes constantdifferences from constantratios. Explicitly requires physicalmechanism and initialcondition, so finite-data nonuniqueness is not concealed.
records.physicalAssumptions: Named Poiseuille model: rigid circular tube, steady fullydeveloped laminar Newtonian incompressible flow, constantviscosity/no-slip and fixed pressure drop/length. Isotropic point-source lossless propagation at fixedpower forinverse-square. Constant attenuationcoefficient anddecayhazard for exponentials, nonnegative interval. Three measurements alone do not identify a unique physical model or license unlimited extrapolation.
